Empirical Research Plan: “The Causal Effect of Attending a Higher-Quality School in Romania”

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. Identification Strategy
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Method: Fuzzy Regression Discontinuity Design (FRD).

Rationale  
• Institutional rule: in the policy reform year, students with an assignment-score above a deterministic cutoff were allotted to a set of “higher-quality” schools; those just below were typically allotted to lower-quality alternatives.  
• Near the cutoff, observed and unobserved characteristics are (by construction) smooth; the only discontinuity is the jump in the probability of attending a high-quality school.  
• Because some families may refuse the assigned school (or appeal), actual attendance is probabilistic ⇒ fuzzy, not sharp, RD.  
• With panel data we can enrich the FRD with “difference-in-RD” (𝑟𝑑×𝑝𝑜𝑠𝑡) or event-study specifications to study dynamics, but the core causal lever is the local comparison at the threshold.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
2. Treatment and Control
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Running variable (R): Assignment score Sᵢ (e.g. composite entrance exam score or distance index) that determines priority.  
Cutoff (c): The official threshold in year t₀ (publicly announced).  

Treatment variable (D): AttendHighᵢ = 1 if student i actually enrolls in a school with a quality index above the median of all schools in the county (or top‐ tercile), 0 otherwise.

• First stage: 𝑑ᵢ = f(Rᵢ ≥ c) + ε (jump in probability of attending a high-quality school).  
• Local treatment group: Students with R just above c (exogenously offered the better school).  
• Local control group: Students with R just below c.  
Treatment timing: first treated school year after assignment (t₀). Outcomes measured annually t₀, t₀+1, … t₀+4 (allows study of persistence).

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
3. Key Identifying Assumptions
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
A1. Continuity of potential outcomes in R at c.  
 Plausibility: assignment score is based on standardized tests; parents cannot perfectly manipulate scores at the single-point level.

A2. No precise manipulation of R around c.  
 Testable via McCrary density test; the Romanian exam uses integer points, grading done centrally → manipulation unlikely but must be checked.

A3. Exclusion / relevance (Fuzzy RD IV): the cutoff affects outcomes only through the increased probability of attending a higher-quality school, and the first-stage jump is strong.  
 Plausible given centralized allocation, but we will quantify the first-stage F-stat.

A4. Stable unit treatment value locally (no spillovers within narrow bandwidth).  
 Within a 2–3 point band, spillover across individuals is minimal because classes are in different schools.

A5. Common support & monotonicity (no one assigned to a worse school because of being above the cutoff).  
 The assignment algorithm is monotone—higher score weakly improves assignment.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
4. Main Threats & Mitigation
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
T1. Precise score manipulation (gaming).  
 • Density test (McCrary).  
 • Balance tests on predetermined covariates (gender, ethnicity, 7th-grade GPA) left and right of c.  
 • If manipulation detected, use donut RD, excluding ±1 point around c.

T2. Differential attrition / delayed enrollment.  
 • Check continuity of “present in data next year” indicator at c.  
 • Re-estimate excluding movers or using inverse-probability weights.

T3. Heterogeneous school capacity constraints (over-subscribed high-quality schools may re-rank using other criteria).  
 • Limit to counties/schools where rule is strictly score-based.  
 • Instrument actual attendance with offer (Z = 1{R≥c}) and estimate local complier effect.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
5. R Code Outline
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
```r
# 0. Packages -----------------------------------------------------------
library(data.table)   # fast data handling
library(fixest)       # OLS and IV
library(rdrobust)     # RD estimation
library(rddensity)    # McCrary density test

# 1. Load & merge yearly files -----------------------------------------
dt <- fread("student_admin_romania.csv")   # one long file or merge beforehand

# 2. Variable construction ---------------------------------------------
dt[, treat_offer   := as.integer(score >= cutoff)]        # Z
dt[, treat_actual  := as.integer(school_quality == "high")] # D
dt[, dist          := score - cutoff]                     # running variable
dt[, within_bw     := abs(dist) <= 5]                     # ±5 points BW example
dt <- dt[!is.na(test_score_nextyr)]                       # keep non-missing outcome

# 3. Descriptive balance (optional) ------------------------------
balance_vars <- c("gender","rural","mother_edu","pretest")
for(v in balance_vars){
  print(feols(get(v) ~ treat_offer, dt[within_bw]))
}

# 4. McCrary density test ---------------------------------------------
dens <- rddensity(dt$score, c = dt$cutoff[1])
summary(dens)

# 5. Fuzzy RD main specification --------------------------------------
# (local polynomial, robust bias-corrected)
frd <- rdrobust(y = dt$test_score_nextyr,
                x = dt$dist,
                c = 0,
                fuzzy = dt$treat_offer)   # Z as fuzzy instrument
summary(frd)

# 6. First stage and reduced form using fixest (local linear, BW=5)
fs  <- feols(treat_actual ~ treat_offer * dist + dist | 0,
             data = dt[within_bw], vcov = "hc1")
rf  <- feols(test_score_nextyr ~ treat_offer * dist + dist | 0,
             data = dt[within_bw], vcov = "hc1")
iv  <- feols(test_score_nextyr ~ 1 | dist + treat_actual ~ treat_offer,
             data = dt[within_bw], vcov = "hc1")
etable(fs, rf, iv)

# 7. Robustness: bandwidth sweep --------------------------------------
for(bw in c(3,4,5,6,7)){
  est <- rdrobust(y = dt$test_score_nextyr,
                  x = dt$dist,
                  c = 0, h = bw,
                  fuzzy = dt$treat_offer)
  print(c(bw, est$coef[1], est$ci[1,]))
}

# 8. Heterogeneity: by parental education ------------------------------
dt[, high_mom := mother_edu >= "high_school"]
est_het <- feols(test_score_nextyr ~ high_mom:treat_actual | dist ~ treat_offer,
                 data = dt[within_bw], vcov = "hc1")
summary(est_het)
```

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
6. Expected Results
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Sign (+): Students marginally assigned to higher-quality schools should score higher on national exams, owing to peer effects, better teachers, and resources.  
Magnitude (prior): International literature finds 0.10–0.20 σ improvement for similar school upgrades. Given Romania’s larger quality gaps, I expect ≈ 0.15–0.25 σ in the first year, maybe attenuating to 0.10 σ by year 3.  
Behavioral response: Some families may increase complementary inputs (e.g., reduce private tutoring if the school is better, or conversely double-down). If tutoring falls by, say, 5 percent, net academic gain could be slightly smaller than pure peer-effect predictions.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
7. Validity Checklist Self-Assessment (RD)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
C1: Clear, known cutoff & strict rule………………1  
C2: No precise manipulation of running variable…1 (pending McCrary)  
C3: Covariate balance at cutoff………………………1  
C4: Strong first stage (relevance)…………………1  
C5: Robustness to bandwidth & polynomial choices…1  

Total = 5 / 5 (subject to empirical verification).
